items.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022
items.q: The first session I was on observing was Stevie Wonder.

ctx.x: Do you remember what you thought about it at the time? I guess it’s as simple asking did you like it?

I did. I enjoyed her creativity. You know it was, you know just to give you a little background going into that, because this is now five years, four years after I started working at Electric Lady and working as an engineer, I had done a lot of stuff just sitting and watching. The first session I was on observing was Stevie Wonder. I mean this is the kind of stuff that was going on there. And great engineers, Bob Margouleff and Malcolm

Cecil, the two guys that were recording and producing Stevie at the time. And I got to sit and watch these guys and they were developing — they were using Moog synthesizers and they had a one called TONTO was the name, and it was these three huge panels of Moog equipment and so forth, and they would work overnight to create a bass sound or whatever they were doing. So there was that, and then another date comes in and it’s John McLaughlin and the Mahavishnu Orchestra. That’s when my life changed. And I was in the…
